headline: High-risk shared-git interaction: Aider can write and modify git state while ai-engineering-hub is an unverified docs-only agent with no isolation, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes repo files and git state, so if ai-engineering-hub’s outputs are copied into the same workspace or repo, malicious instructions can be embedded and later parsed as trusted content. ai-engineering-hub has no documented isolation or I/O surfaces, so the bridge is plausible but not proven. The pairwise pathway is inferred from Aider’s file/git behavior and the other agent’s docs-only profile.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub outputs are pasted into Aider-managed files or commits, injection becomes actionable.
IF both agents share a repo or workspace, attacker-controlled text can traverse the bridge.
mitigations: Keep ai-engineering-hub outputs out of repo files.
Use a separate review-only workspace for Aider inputs.
Require manual diff review before commit.
Strip instruction-like text from upstream outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can egress to configured model providers, while ai-engineering-hub has no documented data-class limits or isolation. If sensitive code or secrets enter the shared repo, Aider may transmit them to third-party inference backends. The exact leak path is indirect, but the pairwise risk exists in default Aider workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared repo, Aider may send their contents to configured model providers.
IF ai-engineering-hub emits secrets or private text into files, those contents can be read by Aider.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared repo.
Use a redacted clone for Aider.
Disable or restrict provider access for sensitive sessions.
Audit git history before sharing the workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data classification gates.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has write_filesystem and modify_git_state with shared-state via a shared git repo, while ai-engineering-hub is an agent-oriented repo artifact with no isolation or locking shown. Concurrent edits to the same repo can overwrite each other or corrupt git state, and Aider’s auto-commit workflow increases the chance of irreversible conflicts. This is a default-dangerous shared-write pattern.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository, write conflicts are possible.
IF Aider auto-commits while ai-engineering-hub also mutates files, git history divergence can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate repos per agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Require manual merge review for every commit.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add repo-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can act on file changes and commit them, so if it consumes ai-engineering-hub outputs as authoritative guidance, errors can cascade into persisted code or repo state. ai-engineering-hub is docs-only and unverified, so its outputs should not be treated as trusted without checks. The pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Aider uses ai-engineering-hub output as instructions without verification, errors can be committed.
IF downstream automation consumes Aider commits, a mistaken upstream output can propagate further.
mitigations: Require human verification of upstream outputs.
Add a validation step before commit.
Limit Aider to draft-only changes.
Review commit messages for unsupported claims.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for ai-engineering-hub, while Aider explicitly handles model-provider API keys and source code. The only concrete compliance concern is that shared code or secrets could be exposed to provider-backed inference, but the profiles do not show a regulated-data mismatch. Because the other agent’s compliance posture is unspecified, this remains low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared repo, provider-backed inference may create a policy issue.
IF ai-engineering-hub is used with data subject to stricter retention rules, review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared repo.
Use a local-only model for sensitive sessions.
Document retention expectations before use.
Review provider terms for the session.
requires-engineering: implement data-residency controls.
